correctness.rationale: For integer m, Le–Rhaly Theorem 2.1 yields positivity of the unshifted defect. The finite-coordinate trace is exactly the off-corner squared matrix mass. The scaled boundary-flux Riemann sum converges with O(1/R) tail control, evaluating to m^2 H_(2m-1)/(2m-1), finite. Positivity then implies actual trace-class membership; a row-nuclear estimate proves M_alpha,m-M_0,m belongs to S1, and trace cyclicity eliminates all cross commutators. Ma Theorem 1.1 supplies the exact negative-part phase boundary, giving trace-norm equality iff alpha>=0. No numerical inference replaces an infinite proof. Depends on cited published all-order interrupter identity and positivity classification.

value.rationale: The trace of a trace-class self-commutator is a canonical nontrivial operator-ideal invariant; the underlying Cesàro matrices are themselves not Hilbert–Schmidt, so finiteness is a substantive cancellation fact. An explicit integer-order harmonic sequence quantifies the invariant and remains constant for every real shift, including shifts where the defect becomes indefinite. The same value is exactly the Schatten-1 norm only on the recent hyponormality range. These features give a motivated structural classification rather than a routine finite table or a cosmetic normalization.
